question: What did the people say about the time to rebuild the house of the LORD, and how were their own houses and harvests?
The adjective חָרֵב (charev, “in ruins”), said of the house in verse 4, sounds like the “drought” of verse 11: what relationship does the prophet suggest between the two?
How do the people and the leaders react to the message, and what does God do before they begin the work?
“Consider your ways” is repeated twice: what are you leaving for later, saying “the time has not yet come”?
How did the older people see the new house compared with the first, and what does God promise about its glory?
The word כָּבוֹד (kavod, “glory”) appears in verses 3, 7 and 9: what kind of glory will the new house have, if not that of size or luxury?
What do the questions about consecrated meat and uncleanness teach about the people's situation before God?
Why is the final promise addressed to Zerubbabel, and what does it mean to be made “like a signet ring”?
“Be strong... for I am with you”: what task before you needs this courage?
